In the given congruence, we have $a=185$ and $n=575$, and we're given that

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(185,575)=5.
$$

Since $b=35$ is divisible by $5,$ our congruence has $5$ solutions.

Next, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}185x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,575) \\ 5\cdot 37x & ≡5\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,5\cdot 115) \\ \cancel{5}\cdot 37x & ≡\cancel{5}\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{5}\cdot 115) \\ 37x & ≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,115)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in this new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=37$ and ${n}_{1}=115$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(37,115)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $115.$

To find the solution, we must multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $37\,(\text{mod}\,115).$ To find the inverse of $37\,(\text{mod}\,115),$ we apply the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}115 & = & 37\cdot 3 & + & 4\, & ⇔ & \,4 & = & 115-37\cdot 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 37 & = & 4\cdot 9 & + & 1\, & ⇔ & \,1 & = & 37-4\cdot 9 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 4 & = & 4\cdot 1 & + & 0\, &  & \, &  & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, back-substituting in the usual way gives the following:

$$
1=28\cdot 37-9\cdot 115
$$

We can write this result in modulo $115,$ as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}28\cdot 37-9\cdot 115 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,115) \\ 28\cdot 37 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,115)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse of $37$ modulo $115$ is $28.$

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $28,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}37x & ≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,115) \\ 28\cdot 37x & ≡28\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,115) \\ x & ≡196 &  & (\text{mod}\,115) \\ x & ≡115\cdot 1+81 &  & (\text{mod}\,115) \\ x & ≡81 &  & (\text{mod}\,115)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡81\,(\text{mod}\,115).$

But our original congruence was modulo $575$ (not modulo $115$). To find all the solutions modulo $575,$ we repeatedly add $115$ to $81$ modulo $575$ until we reach the number $81$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡81 &  & (\text{mod}\,575) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡81+115≡196 &  & (\text{mod}\,575) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡196+115≡311 &  & (\text{mod}\,575) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡311+115≡426 &  & (\text{mod}\,575) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡426+115≡541 &  & (\text{mod}\,575) \\ {x}_{6} & ≡541+115≡656≡575+81≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,575)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2,3,4,5}≡81,\,196,\,311,\,426,\,541\,(\text{mod}\,575).
$$
